bugs.description: best-response-p1 (and best-response-p2) will crash with an error if the game has no strategies for a player, because 'apply max' is called on an empty list.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Add a check for null payoffs or ensure the game has at least one strategy per player before computing best response.

bugs.description: best-response-p1 and best-response-p2 use 'list-ref' inside a 'filter' over the same list, resulting in O(n^2) complexity where O(n) is possible. This makes 'find-pure-nash' O(n^4).
bugs.fix_suggestion: Iterate through the payoffs and indices together using a named let or use vectors for constant-time access during the filtering phase.

bugs.description: solve-2x2-nash uses exact equality (=) and strict boundary checks (>= 0, <= 1) for floating point probabilities p and q. Rounding errors may cause valid mixed equilibria to be rejected (e.g., if q computes to 1.0000000000000002).
bugs.fix_suggestion: Use a small epsilon for boundary checks and equality comparisons, e.g., (and (> q -epsilon) (< q (+ 1 epsilon))).

bugs.description: solve-2x2-nash explicitly excludes equilibria where p or q are 0 or 1. While these are often pure equilibria, in degenerate games, mixed equilibria can exist where one player mixes and the other plays a pure strategy; these are missed by this logic.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Allow p and q to be 0 or 1 in the mixed strategy calculation, or handle degenerate cases where denominators are zero more comprehensively.

bugs.description: eliminate-strategy-p1 uses (filter (lambda (x) x) ...) to remove a strategy. This will incorrectly remove any strategy name that happens to be the boolean #f.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Filter by index instead of value, or use a unique sentinel value that cannot be a strategy name.

bugs.description: qty-pow uses 'expt' on the quantity value. If the value is 0 and the exponent n is negative, this will cause a division-by-zero error.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Add a check for zero value when the exponent is negative and handle or error gracefully.

bugs.description: qty-sqrt applies 'sqrt' to the quantity value without checking for negative values. While mathematically valid (returning complex numbers), it may be unexpected for physical units where magnitudes are typically non-negative.
bugs.fix_suggestion: Consider adding a check for negative values if the library is intended for strictly real-valued physical quantities.
